topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series and sets out what students should learn before substantive teaching begins.

topics.label: Accumulating genetic and epigenetic changes in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces cancer development as a stepwise accumulation of cellular changes and identifies the questions this model raises.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of differentiation and tissue organisation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer through the disruption of organised tissue development, showing why studying isolated cells cannot fully capture that disruption.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign and malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish invasion as the defining distinction between benign and malignant tumors and develop its histological and prognostic implications.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumor names communicate tissue of origin and malignant status, including exceptions to the naming conventions.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumor growth disrupts normal bodily function and why metastatic disease is especially lethal.

topics.label: Tumor incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the occurrence of tumor types across populations and species to establish the distribution of cancer.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how screening seeks to detect treatable disease before clinical presentation and why its effectiveness varies between cancers.

topics.label: Lecture close and follow-up
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by directing students back to the learning outcomes and ahead to revision and practicals.
